children: ADIA offloads 3.5 crore Lenskart shares for Rs 2,390.6 crore as the eyewear company's stock rallies 51.3 per cent year-to-date Lenskart, ADIA, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Platinum Jasmine, block deal, Rs 2,390.6 crore, stake sale, eyewear, Q1 FY27, stock market, SoftBank, Temasek, Alpha Wave
Early investor Abu Dhabi Investment Authority has offloaded 3.5 crore shares of eyewear company Lenskart through its holding entity Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, as per a media report.

The shares were sold at Rs 683.02 apiece, generating proceeds of Rs 2,390.6 crore through the bulk deal. The transaction came at a price slightly below Lenskart's closing price of Rs 683.85 on the NSE.
This marks the second instance of ADIA reducing its stake in Lenskart in recent months. In June, the investor sold 4 crore shares in a block deal worth Rs 1,960 crore.
The June transaction valued Lenskart shares at Rs 490 apiece, around 40 per cent below the latest closing price.

At the end of the June quarter, Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust held 16.98 crore Lenskart shares, representing a 9.77 per cent stake in the company. The latest sale accounts for slightly over 20 per cent of ADIA's holding and around 2 per cent of Lenskart's total equity.

Lenskart's shares have gained 51.3 per cent on a year-to-date basis, providing an opportunity for several early investors to monetise their holdings. SoftBank, Temasek and Alpha Wave have also sold shares in the company in recent months.
In September, BNP Paribas, Societe Generale and US-based hedge fund Millennium Management sold Lenskart shares worth Rs 2,670.2 crore through multiple bulk deals.
Lenskart touched an all-time high of Rs 725 on 18 September. The company made its stock market debut at Rs 390 per share on the BSE in November 2025.

The stock's recent rally followed positive brokerage commentary after Lenskart reported strong Q1 FY27 results. Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 680 from Rs 600, while Macquarie increased its target to Rs 675 from Rs 625.

Lenskart's consolidated net profit jumped 273 per cent year-on-year to Rs 228.4 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 61.2 crore a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 43 per cent year-on-year and 8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 2,714.2 crore.
However, Lenskart shares closed 3.3 per cent lower at Rs 683.85 on the NSE.
